facts.raw_span: A full-term girl presented at birth with multiple skin lesions
One month later, she returned due to recurring skin eruptions
Multiple areas of erythema, vesicles, and bullae on the face, trunk, and extremities
Vital signs including temperature, respiration, and heart rate were within normal ranges
Multiple round or irregularly shaped erythematous macules and slightly scaly plaques of various sizes on face, trunk, and extremities
Bullous and vesicular lesions on thighs, with scattered facial erosions
Mucous membranes not affected
thickened, brown, corrugated plaques over neck, armpits, wrists, and ankles, along with palmoplantar hyperkeratosis

Skin-punch biopsy: Revealed hyperkeratosis, distinct vacuolization in the granular and upper spinous layers, and bullae formation within the epidermis, with sparse inflammatory cells in the superficial dermis
Direct immunofluorescence (DIF): Results were unremarkable
Whole-exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous variation c.482T>C (p. L161P) in KRT1
Hyperkeratotic plaques with distinct borders and annular appearance
Shows hyperkeratosis, spinous cell vacuolization, and vesicles in the epidermis

concepts.why: The patient's skin lesions, erythema, and hyperkeratosis, along with the genetic variation in KRT1, support this diagnosis.
The patient's skin lesions, erythema, and hyperkeratosis, along with the genetic variation in KRT1, support this diagnosis, although it is less specific than epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.
The patient's genetic variation in KRT1 supports this diagnosis, which is a broader category of disorders related to keratin mutations.
The patient's recurring skin eruptions and erythema in the first month of life support this diagnosis, although it is less specific than other diagnoses.
The patient's palmoplantar hyperkeratosis supports this diagnosis, which is a specific type of keratoderma.

rationales.F08: The presence of thickened, brown, corrugated plaques and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis is highly suggestive of Epidermolytic hyperkeratosis and Keratinopathy.
rationales.F09: The skin-punch biopsy results revealing hyperkeratosis, vacuolization, and bullae formation are characteristic of Epidermolytic hyperkeratosis and Keratinopathy.
rationales.F11: The genetic testing revealing a heterozygous variation in KRT1 is highly suggestive of Epidermolytic hyperkeratosis and Keratinopathy.
rationales.F12: The presence of hyperkeratotic plaques with distinct borders and annular appearance is highly suggestive of Epidermolytic hyperkeratosis and Keratinopathy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's skin lesions, hyperkeratosis, and bullae formation are consistent with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis, and the genetic testing revealed a heterozygous variation in KRT1, which is a common cause of this condition.
